function: Joint AP precoding and IRS phase-shift design maximizing weighted sum rate; NAS-built PhaseNet outputs IRS phases and BeamNet outputs precoders from channels (p. 3-5, 9)
system: IRS-aided downlink MU-MISO: AP with M=8 antennas, K=4 single-antenna users, reflecting IRS with N=100 continuous-phase elements, 180 kHz bandwidth; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 9, 10)
method: NTK-guided neural architecture search of cascaded PhaseNet and BeamNet, with AO-generated labels and Bayesian optimization; the chosen network is trained unsupervised on negative weighted sum rate (p. 4-9)
data_channel: Own Rician channels (kappa=10) with 3GPP path loss; Monte Carlo data: 20,000 AO-labeled instances for the search, then 60,000 instances with 20,000 reserved for testing (p. 10)
test_conditions: Train and test on the same setting (M=8, N=100, K=4, 10 dBm), 20,000 test instances; one parameter varied at a time, retraining not stated (p. 10-12)
baselines: Classical: BCD [1], upper bound, random phase with WMMSE, no IRS; learned: CFNN [17], DQNN [15], GNN [12], deep-unfolding DUFD (p. 11)
metrics: Weighted sum rate; validation loss; Kendall tau and Spearman rho of NTK metrics versus validation loss (p. 10-12)
complexity: Search cost O(C|P| + tau T_v) (Eq. 20), equal to O(T_s(|P|/(bE) + tau/6)) (p. 9); no FLOPs, parameters or runtime of the found networks
q1_support: p. 10: "a Rician channel model is adopted for the channels"; the 3GPP mention ("comply with the 3GPP propagation environment standards") covers only the path-loss parameters of Table I. No CDL/TDL, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "only one parameter is adjusted at a time" in the sweeps of Fig. 10; the paper does not state that a network trained in one setting is tested in another, and it credits BNAS with adaptively refining its architecture as the input dimensions grow.
q3_support: p. 11: "BNAS not only exhibits superior performance over BCD" and "the BNAS framework consistently outperforms other DL-based methods across all scenarios"; CFNN [17], DQNN [15] and GNN [12] are earlier learned baselines, compared on weighted sum rate (Fig. 10).
q4_support: p. 9: "thus, the total complexity is" O(C|P| + tau T_v) (Eq. 20), the order of the architecture search; no FLOPs, parameter count or runtime of the found networks is reported.
q5_support: p. 10: "Multiple Monte Carlo simulations are performed according to [1] to generate the dataset"; the data are the authors' own simulation labeled by the AO algorithm, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Published version, IEEE TWC 2026, pp. 1155-1168. Area 3: NAS builds the networks that output IRS phases and precoders for weighted sum rate. Tables I-II (p. 10) and Fig. 10 (p. 12) were read from page images. q1 is 0: Rician channels with only the path-loss parameters from 3GPP. q2 is 0 under the explicit-statement rule: Fig. 10 varies N, power, K, phase bits, NMSE and Rician factor one at a time, but the paper does not say whether one trained network is tested in another setting or retrained; the reviewer may check Fig. 10 and p. 11. q4 is 1 for the order of the architecture search cost (Eq. 20, p. 9), a design cost; no FLOPs, parameters or runtime of the found network are given, so the reviewer may decide whether this counts.
